newsitem.title: FRANCE: UNSA union joins French civil service pay protest.
newsitem.headline: UNSA union joins French civil service pay protest.

text.p: The UNSA civil service trade union group joined the CGT union in condemning a French government pay offer to public employees on Tuesday.
It said it would call on all unions to give the offer the "response it merits".

Unions had warned in advance of the pay offer presentation on Tuesday that they would consider a strike if it fell short of their demands, especially for a "catch-up" reward to compensate for a 1996 pay freeze.
The unions saw Civil Service Minister Dominique Perben one-by-one to hear the pay offer.
The CGT broke the news that Perben was proposing a pay rise of 2.8 percent over 1997-1998 and that there was no offer concerning a catch-up for 1996.
The unions meet on Tuesday evening at 1800 GMT.

"After freezing salaries for more than a year and keeping us waiting as it delayed opening of pay negotiations from one month to another, the government has chopped the talks off at the root just when they were supposed to start," an UNSA statement said.
Like the CGT, the UNSA union said the government's position was at odds with President Jacques Chirac's declarations that 1997 should be a year of social dialogue.
The offer was the result of a general government policy of tightening the belt to prepare for European monetary union.
"These choices are unacceptable. They are dangerous because they are destructive for the economy, and thus employment," it said. -- Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
